data.authority: Synthetic organization administrative procedure; any CMS facts are separately identified.
data.local_policy: The office’s ordinary-redetermination release uses the actual verified notice receipt when available. The appeals deadline team supplies a supported good-cause account or other timing position for an officer-authorized late filing. This task’s send_appeal action represents immediate electronic receipt on the assignment date, not a mailed dispatch. The MAC, rather than the assistant, decides an extension for good cause.

cms_source.locator: Ch29 §240; §310.2; First Level of Appeal, Requesting a Redetermination
cms_source.rule: The filing period is 120 days from receipt; verified receipt overrides the five-day presumption. Nonworkday rollover and good-cause extensions can apply.

handoff_requirement: Use the actual verified June 9 receipt to identify the 120-day ordinary deadline of October 7, a recorded working day. State that the October 8 assignment has missed that window and lacks a good-cause account or extension decision. Urgently request the deadline team’s supported timing/good-cause review and officer-authorized filing plan; do not call the appeal permanently barred.

data.text: More than 120 days have elapsed since the notice date.
data.alert_basis: Notice issue date plus 120 calendar days

rule_provenance: CMS Claims Processing Manual ch29 §240 and §310.2 (https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/clm104c29.pdf); First Level of Appeal, Requesting a Redetermination (https://www.cms.gov/medicare/appeals-grievances/fee-for-service/first-level-appeal-redetermination-medicare-contractor). The supported actual receipt controls; working-calendar dates are synthetic facts. Late-filing review remains possible and is not a permanent appeal prohibition.
